author: Frobatim
title: Weird vibes!
text:
This was such a weird hotel. Lobby was the most visually appealing part. The hallways are dark and cramped. As a woman, this was creepy!

Gave it the benefit of the doubt bc the AM staff was wonderful! Brandon and Hero (I think this was his name) were super welcoming. The two stars are for them! 

My room was ready at 9am which I wasn’t expecting so that was a plus. 

3 stars removed for the extremely small room. Cover is extremely thin. PM staff was a bit strange, almost unapproachable. AND they advertise like 3 different restaurants / bars and you can’t even charge it to the room! Wtf.

Also, they charged me the for 2 nights and the incidental fee of $200 which was fine but there was an additional charge for $278. Apparently this was a preauthorization charge. Very strange bc if the charge for the room went through, what’s the preauth for? I asked about it and they immediately returned it. Imagine if I didn’t ask.

All in all, if you just need to sleep fine. But there’s 20+ hotels in the area to choose from. Avoid this one.

author: FrenchGarden
title: Restful stay in Manhattan: practical room and cozy vibe
text: I had an excellent stay at this hotel. My premium room was comfortable and very practical—there was easily enough space to leave my suitcase open without it getting in the way! The air conditioning worked perfectly, so there was no need to run the additional window unit. The Wi-Fi was strong, the bed was comfortable, and the bathroom was in pristine, recently renovated condition with powerful shower pressure. Overall, the room had a very restful & cosy atmosphere.

author: Cameron P
title: Brandon at Freehand
text: Brandon at freehand was really dope and kind to us.

author: David S
title: Good service and convenient
text: A good convenient overnight. Javier at the desk helped with Q’s and getting a king bed on the quiet side of the hotel.  The staff at bars and cafe - totally professional.  It’s a good location for walking to downtown and catching the subway.  BTW - amazing water pressure in the shower.

author: 235Ale
title: Disappointing
text:
We spent 5 nights in a room with a king-size bed.

Pros:
1) very convenient location for visiting Manhattan;
2) very kind reception staff.

Cons:

1) Very noisy room. You could clearly hear noises coming from the neighboring rooms and the hallway and, above all, those from the street, which was very busy at all hours, particularly early in the morning.
2) Small and poorly organized room. A disproportionate part of the space is occupied by the kitchen, which for short stays can be of little use (in our case we did not use it at all). Paradoxically, there is no table with chairs where you could eat even just a sandwich. The wardrobe was tiny (about half a meter wide) and already partly occupied by the ironing board, iron, and hair dryer; furthermore, there was no specific space for suitcases.
3) Inadequate cleaning service. Out of a five-day stay, on two separate occasions we returned in the evening, after a full day out, and found the room not made up and the towels not changed.
4) Exasperatingly slow elevator, which is also shared with the service staff. More than once, after a long wait, the elevator finally arrived but was completely occupied by staff and therefore unusable by guests.
5) Breakfast room definitely too small for the number of guests. Having breakfast becomes a stressful race to manage to find one of the few available tables.
6) I find the choice to give the same name, TownePlace Suites, to two different hotels located in the same area of Manhattan incomprehensible. It is a completely avoidable source of confusion, with the risk of unpleasant inconveniences. A hotel, which by definition welcomes people from out of town, should do everything possible to provide clear and unambiguous directions.

We will not return, and we will advise others against coming to this hotel.

author: mkbnj
title: Great location, good price for midtown, but lots of flaws
text:
I wanted to like this location. We visit Birdland, across the street, a few times a year. Unfortunately, there were several issues to kick this review down to average, maybe below average.

On the positive side, staff are great; the room is clean with newer and comfortable bedding, newer furnishings and recently remodeled bathroom.  The included breakfast had oatmeal, cereal, eggs, sausage, ham and cheese sandwich, small yogurts and actually good coffee. The location is superb, and the price was very attractive for midtown.

On the negative side, the room is small (the website claims 260 sq ft, more like 200), I reserved a king size bed and the room was a queen size with visibly less space than the website picture  (several other reviews here had the same experience with that, what's going on?), I was on the 7th floor, two rooms away from the elevator, but all night long and especially in the morning, hear a mechanical clang-clung-clang every time the elevator stopped on a floor, I could not sleep; the a/c thermostat was defective so that the room setting was a high point and would cool the room down 5 degrees before shutting cooling, so sleeping was either very cold or very hot - a mechanic, who did not understand or speak English very well, drained the a/c of water and left, not fixing the thermostat issue; breakfast fruit was just a small apple and there are tables for about 15 people, so I inconveniently ate on a sofa; the elevator is painfully slow and tests your patience.

author: mwgoldstein
title: Staff is great, and it’s clean, butttttt….
text:
It’s really difficult for me to give this place anything better than a mediocre review. 

First, the good: Hotel staff are friendly and helpful. Also, the location is close to Times Square but not too close. Everything was clean…room, bed, shower…very important, especially in NYC where cleanliness can’t be assumed.

Now, the bad: Everything is cramped. Lobby is small. Breakfast area is tiny. There’s only 5-6 tables in the breakfast area. Breakfast itself was mediocre at best. There’s one elevator. It’s painfully slow and makes banging sounds at every floor. Only seven floors in this building, but it’ll take you forever to get to/from your room. Once you make it to your room, prepare to be cramped. It’s so small, we questioned if it was actually smaller than a basic cruise ship room. There’s no space to do anything. Water pressure in the shower is too weak. Our first night was painfully hot. Maintenance came but couldn’t fix the AC. We later found out the AC was out on the entire 7th floor and wouldn’t be fixed until the morning. Management didn’t fight me the next morning when I asked to have the first night taken off the bill. Guess that should go up in the “good” section.

Kudos to the staff for making the best out of a building they have to know has a lot of issues, so at least there’s that. It’d take a lot for me to stay there again.

author: soho6102
title: Decent Value Option
text:
The hotel’s location was one of its biggest advantages. It was conveniently located just a couple of blocks from Penn Station, Times Square, and many other popular New York City attractions, making it easy to get around the city.

When I arrived, I was quickly greeted by the front desk attendant and had a smooth check-in experience. One thing to note is that this is a very small hotel. There is only one elevator, and it is extremely slow. If you don’t mind waiting, it’s manageable, but it definitely became an inconvenience during my stay. The elevator was working, but I often chose to take the stairs instead, walking down four floors and up three floors each day, which became a bit frustrating.

The room itself was very clean, neat, and seemed well maintained. I appreciated the small suite-style kitchenette, which was a convenient feature and gave the room a little more functionality, especially for a longer stay.

However, I did encounter an issue with the bathroom. There appeared to be a small gnat issue or nest in the shower drain area, with several gnats flying around. It was annoying and, in my opinion, raised some concerns about cleanliness and hygiene perhaps with the city drain. I contacted the front desk to see if there were any other rooms available, but the hotel was fully booked during my stay, so I had to remain in the same room.

The hotel does offer complimentary breakfast, which included items such as sausage, eggs, bagels, oatmeal, and coffee. It was nothing elaborate, but it was a nice convenience to have available. I only used the breakfast once during my stay since it wasn’t really the type of meal I normally eat, but I appreciated the option.

Overall, this hotel is a decent choice for travelers looking to save a little money while staying in the heart of Manhattan. The location is excellent, and the rooms are clean and functional. However, due to the extremely slow elevator and the gnat issue in my bathroom, I would probably not choose this particular location again for a future New York City stay.

author: Brian W
title: Very Basic with VERY SLOW elevator in the front
text:
I am a marriott titanium so I think I've stayed at a wide gamut of their hotel brands.  This is my first Towneplace and I was prepared for it to be like a residence inn or similar brands.  Yes it was but I can say it didnt necessarily meet up to standards.  This is a smaller hotel in a very convenient location to times square.  I never felt it was noisy and it was clean.  
There are two different sections of the hotel; front and back (back faces 43rd st).  When I checked in I stayed in the front of the hotel in a reserved king room.  I asked for any upgraded rooms and they said there were none available.  After getting the keys it took 3 or 4 minutes for the elevator to arrive.  MIND YOU the hotel is maybe 5 or 6 stories so this is unacceptable.  Got to the room and it was a queen.  Went to the front desk and they said according to the computer it was a king.  I said you're more than welcome to come to the room and see it was a queen bed.  At this point it really didnt matter since I was told it was sold out and we can try to move you the next day.
The next day at 8am I went to the front desk and the person behind the desk was very pleasant and nice and said I can give you the larger room which has a king and is handicap accessible.  I took it.  This room was in the back hotel and the elevators actually worked and didnt take more than a minute to arrive.  THe room was much nicer.
The breakfast was basic and decent...exactly what I was expecting.  Also beware the front doors to the hotel auto locks at 7pm.  That's a little early for the times square area.  I never felt unsafe so not sure why that was even necessary
Lastly, I wish I could post on the marriott website, but you need to be invited to leave a review.  I relied on the above 4 star rating to book this hotel, but it really is a 3 star and I would have selected a different hotel.

author: Waymond Ho
title: Small but convenient location
text: The room was a bit small and tight, but the location is right around the corner from all Earl's Court Station transportation choices.  Lots of good selection of convenience stores and restaurants around it too. The staff were courteous and efficient.  The bed in our room was really soft and one should be careful when getting close to the edge as you will roll off. Their continental breakfast is OK but nothing special.

author: Roman C
title: Overbooking. Cancelled 2 hours before arrived
text: Stay away from this hotel. I booked a room there a few days before my trip. A couple of days later, they asked for confirmation that I would definitely be arriving, which I provided. On the day of arrival, two hours before I was due to get there, I received a message from Booking.com stating that there was no accommodation for me. By that time, I had already been on the train for four hours and had two hours of the journey left. Booking.com isn't any better either, so I advise being careful with them.

author: Inspire28016730800
title: Not a trustworthy place !
text:
A very upsetting and unsettling experience. This is not a trustworthy hotel. They cancelled my confirmed reservation without my consent, leaving me with no clear explanation and no support. This is not correct. 

To make matters worse, I noticed that the exact room I had booked was listed again shortly afterwards, but at a much higher price.
Therefore, I would strongly advise others to book elsewhere.

author: Rebecca P
title: Fabulous stay with a lovely touch
text:
Stayed for one night with my daugher. I emailed the hotel to ask if we could check in early as we had a 4pm pre theatre reservation for my daughters 21st. 
They replied back straight away saying they had noted this on the booking and would try and accommodate if possible.
We arrived at 1pm and room was ready. The most lovely touch was a box of M&S biscuits and a birthday card for my daugher was waiting in the room.
Really friendly staff, great location with a tube station 3 minute walk away. 
Lovely well equipped, clean rooms.
Thank you for a wonderful stay and the biscuits.
Will use again and recommend.

author: Selfie M
title: Total scammed hotel
text:
This hotel is totally scam.
I have done booking and it’s confirmed by hotel but when i reached to hotel for check in they said your booking is cancelled without any reason, i have got my friends came from canada to visit uk and the scammed us, we have no where else to because all the hotel was full in central London and its not only us they scammed everyone who came at that day.

author: sbirulina71
title: Excellent location
text: Cute, clean hotel, excellent location for visiting the city on foot. Good value for money. Varied, abundant breakfast with the option of takeout. Kind and courteous. I would return.

author: Annemarie R
title: Good location
text: 5 nights stay. Outside, a part of the staff who also berated us said 'shame on you' because we were staying there. Not very nice. The staff who did work did their best. The lying is good. Breakfast was really mediocre with little choice.

author: Martina M
title: New York
text: Good hotel near Times Square, clean.  The reception staff is very friendly. Elevators a bit slow, as there are few compared to the number of users. Breakfast is so-so, with too many people at any time. However, I would stay there again.

author: Marco S
title: GOOD EXPERIENCE
text:
Hotel very close to Time Square, friendly staff at reception. Average rooms, a little small but you survive, super crowded breakfast room, but we always found food that was readily replenished just finished at the buffet. Lifts a bit slow, in fact to go to the highest floors there are only two.
However to recommend.

author: well_traveled
title: Uncomfortable and unwelcoming.
text: Avoid at all cost. Management were silent on complaints I brought up during my stay. They respond here but won't return calls. Dirty and Dumpy and rooms that didn't get cleaned. Avoid.

author: Mirko
title: Just perfect
text: Just perfect. The service is great and also it’s clean and has the best location to stay. Directly at Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park you can do nearly everything without getting in the tube or at the bus. It’s awesome. The rooms are great designed and you have everything there for a great stay. The people who working there are always friendly and work with a smile and helps you at everything. All together…we will definitely come back soon and was the best stay in London you can think about

author: David R
title: Still no refund
text:
Had a good stay at NOX Waterloo and hoping for the same. Booked a room with air conditioning months in advance but just provided with a fan and no air con. Complained and asked to be moved but no other rooms available. 34 degrees and the room was unbearable. Moved on the second night to a basement room which was fine.

Complained a number of times and eventually got the offer of a £50 refund. Still waiting for this a month after the offer.

author: TuyetNhi N
title: Personal belongings went missing after luggage storage.
text:
The location of the hotel is very good. It is within walking distance of both Queensway and Bayswater Underground stations, making it easy to get around London.
We were staying in the jacuzzi suite the room itself was okay, but there were several things that could easily be improved. Although there was a kitchenette, there was no tea towel or dish towel, making it difficult to wash and dry dishes. We were only given large bath towels, with no hand towels or smaller towels for our face or hair. We asked the staff if they could provide smaller towels, but they told us they didn’t have any. There was also only one chair in the room, so whenever we wanted to have breakfast together, one of us had to sit on the bed, which was quite inconvenient.
The check-out experience was also disappointing. We were not asked how our stay had been or whether everything was okay. Instead, the receptionist simply asked for our key card.
The biggest issue, however, happened after our stay. We stored our luggage at the hotel after checking out. Before leaving our luggage there, I still had my AirPods. Afterwards, they went missing. When I checked Apple’s Find My app, the AirPods remained at the hotel location after we had left. Later that evening, at around 10:00 PM, the location started moving and has since remained at the same residential address. I contacted the hotel immediately, but the only response I received was that housekeeping had thoroughly cleaned the room and found nothing. They also advised me to file a police report, which I intend to do.
I also came across several reviews from other guests mentioning missing belongings after leaving their luggage in the hotel’s luggage storage. While I cannot say with certainty what happened, the timeline shown in the Find My app, combined with my experience, has made this situation extremely concerning and frustrating.
Because of this experience, I will not be returning to this hotel. I would advise other travellers to keep a close eye on their valuables and carefully consider whether they want to leave their luggage in storage here.

author: MrsWelly
title: Not conducive to a restful night sleep
text: Whilst attractive, not conducive to a decent night’s sleep with a continuous running toilet however many times I tried to flush.   Gas light by the operating company who said they could not verify a fault, after ‘we carried out an investigation into the issue’  - how was this possible within 18 minutes of receiving my email.   Keep searching for a better place to stay if you are in the area

author: Dawn H
title: Excellent
text: Location was perfect few minutes walk from Queensway Underground station. Staff very friendly helpful, room and hotel was clean and well equipped

author: Islandtime11
title: Experience it! YOLO
text: The negative reviews are not wrong, BUT, glamping is still a form of camping, therefore, it is not a hotel where you can expect things to be a certain way. Meaning, remember that you will be outdoors on an island next to a major city, you are sleeping on a comfy bed on wood planks over grass! You did not need to pitch your own tent, it was cleaned and set up for you - with AC, 2 fans, a normal flushing toilet, rain shower, spacious vanity, plenty of seating and room to move around comfortably. (full length mirror was an unexpected bonus!)  And as far as the staff, keep in mind that they do not stay there overnight, they commute there each day. The King Waterfront Voyager tent is the way to go. We were in tent #3 with a great view of the Statue of Liberty and far enough away from the main lawn/restaurants/construction which made us feel like we were in our own little world. You are paying for the view and proximity to NYC. It is experience that we will never forget. It helped that we had perfect weather too. Bring books, games, things to keep you busy as there are no TVs.

author: daniel k
title: Three Chances. Three Disappointments. Never Again.
text:
This starts with a year ago, I booked a stay at Collective Retreats on Governors Island as a graduation gift for my niece and her best friend, who were traveling down from upstate New York.

The day they arrived to check in, they were told there were no tents or cabins available because the entire property had been booked for a wedding. Collective seemed confused as to why we had never been notified. Eventually they blamed a “system glitch” that supposedly prevented us from receiving any cancellation notice or refund.

What made this even more frustrating was that they had sent both a welcome email and a reservation confirmation just days before check-in. Naturally, we assumed everything was on schedule.

As a result, my niece and her friend were stranded in New York City with nowhere to stay. They had traveled all the way from upstate expecting a confirmed reservation. I called Collective and insisted they find them a hotel for the night. I actually had to beg them to book any hotel room in NYC for the peace of mind knowing they’re safe. Evan from Collective agreed and arranged a room.

Unfortunately, the problems continued.

Evan assured me that my credit card would only be used for incidental charges. Instead, I was charged for both the hotel room and the incidentals. After I provided Collective with my credit card statement and the hotel invoice proving the charges, they agreed to reimburse me—but it took nearly three months to get my money back.

Despite that experience, I had always wanted to stay overnight on Governors Island. For my birthday, I decided to give Collective another chance.

They canceled that reservation too.

At least this time they notified me in advance.

Against my better judgment, I made a third reservation for a different week. This time I actually made it to check-in.

Unfortunately, the customer service left a lot to be desired.

I asked where the restrooms were and was simply told to walk down a rocky path. There were no signs—just rows of tents. I wasn’t comfortable opening random tent doors, unsure whether they were guest accommodations or restrooms. I walked back to the front desk for clarification.

The staff member responded, “Use your listening ears,” as though I simply hadn’t been paying attention.

I calmly explained that I am legally deaf in my left ear. That comment was both rude and unprofessional. Only then did she personally walk me to the restrooms—which honestly should have been the response from the beginning, especially considering there is no signage directing guests nor any signage at the restrooms.

Dinner wasn’t much better. We ordered pasta and grilled fish. About 30 minutes later, after we’d already been waiting, we were told the fish had sold out. That pretty much summed up the experience.

Throughout our stay, most of the staff appeared unhappy and disengaged. Even simple requests, like asking for a golf cart ride, were met with visible annoyance, making us feel like we were inconveniencing them.

The location itself is beautiful, and Governors Island is a wonderful place to visit. That’s what makes this experience so disappointing. After three separate bookings—two cancellations, one leaving my family stranded, reimbursement issues, and poor service during the stay—I can’t recommend Collective Retreats. There are simply too many operational problems and too little customer care to justify the premium price.

author: SnappleSpice
title: Summer camp, not luxury
text:
I’ve had several “glamping” experiences that could be defined as luxurious, but this wasn’t one of them. It wasn’t a terrible stay, and even as a native New Yorker the city views at night from Governors Island still feel incredible. I spent one night here with a friend, and I’m glad we did it but I wont be back.

For starters, the staff were all friendly and accommodating and I don’t think any of the issues at the camp are their fault. It seems that this company uses the unique location as their main selling point but doesn’t bother to pay attention to the smaller details. 

Upon arriving to Governors Island, we did see a golf cart ready to transport people to the camp, as expected (we were in communication about arrival time). However, there were six people going to the camp from our ferry and only four seats. My friend and I had to wait (in the rain) for the golf cart to drop off the first guests, and then drive back to pick us up. 

Our tent was as expected, and comfortable. The beds felt clean and the AC kept things cool. The shower was, however, freezing as we didn’t have hot water. We were right next to the lobby tent, which made walking to dinner easy. The dinner itself was expensive and bland, although we ate during happy hour and were able to get two cocktails for $20 total (a good price for NYC). 

I’m familiar with Governors Island, so I expected the near constant noise of helicopters and ferries, but there was also a lot of noise from construction that is happening right next to the camp. The campsite doesn’t feel very private or secluded.

After dinner we asked to be driven to the nearby QCNY spa. We were dropped off, and later picked up, without any issues. It had been raining earlier, so unfortunately the campfires were not happening. In other glamping sites I have stayed at, when activities are canceled they do their best to reschedule or modify - for example, indoor s’mores - but no such thing happened here. We were simply told no (by a random staff member working the bar area - no signs, no communication). Again, no attention to smaller details that could make a big impact on a guests’ stay.

The following morning we woke up ready for yoga, but there were no signs indicating where it might be. Both my friend and I attempted to text the front desk (once we saw no one was working it), but never got a response. We walked around the entire campsite after a staff member vaguely pointed across the site and said she thinks it might be in one of the tents. As we started to head back, we noticed one of the tents had games outside of it. We trekked through the muddy grounds and finally found the yoga, although by this point we were late.

The yoga itself was run by Samantha and it was absolutely the highlight of our stay! It was a great relaxing session that worked in a few challenging moves so my friend and I could get some cool pictures. Samantha clearly cares deeply about her practice and is very good at what she does! 

The breakfast was very disappointing. The one cabinet holding a few pastries was broken, and there was a single large bowl of fruit, a few yogurts, and a bowl of hard boiled eggs that had run out before we got a chance to have any. It was super casual, disposable materials, and absolutely the bare minimum. 

Even check-out felt bumpy. We brought our stuff to the front desk at check-out time, and no one was there. A few other people were also standing around waiting. Again, no one responded to any of the texts we sent. Finally, someone did arrive to check us out, and then drive us back to the ferry.

Overall, this cost way more than it should have. The location is unique, and the yoga session was fantastic, but other than that this place was disappointing. A few small changes could make this place feel luxurious but instead it just felt like a kids summer camp.

author: Nusrat P
title: Stay at the Aliz
text:
The hotel is in a good location and within walking distance of Broadway and Times Square. There are also plenty of coffee shops, food stops, money exchange places and other conveniences nearby. A 7-Eleven is just a stone’s throw from the hotel, which is very convenient.

The rooms are on the small side but come with a coffee machine and a steam iron for your clothes. The rooms are quite dark, and the lighting could definitely be better. The air conditioning is also very noisy and loud. Unfortunately, the beds are quite uncomfortable, as are the pillows, but if you are mainly using the hotel as somewhere to sleep, then it is manageable.

Breakfast is fairly standard and nothing too exciting. The hotel provides one $25 token per room, which can be spent on beverages or put towards breakfast or dinner. Breakfast costs $35, so you have to pay the difference, which isn’t too bad. Alternatively, you can buy drinks, snacks and other bits and pieces from the downstairs bar using your token. 

The hotel also has a good viewpoint on the 40th floor. However, if you are travelling with children, they cannot access the viewpoint because you have to be 21 or over due to the bar being located there.

You are provided with two complimentary bottles of water per day per room, with no extras included. If you need more water, you can fill up bottles from the fountain on the lower ground floor or buy your own.

Housekeeping was good throughout our stay. Overall, we had a good stay and the location is definitely one of the hotel’s biggest advantages.

One thing to mention is that some of the reception staff can be quite abrasive. However, there were also staff members who were very helpful. In particular, there was one guy at reception with blonde highlights in his hair who was extremely helpful, although unfortunately I can’t remember his name.

Overall, I would say this is a good hotel if location and convenience are your priorities. The rooms and beds could be more comfortable, and the lighting and air conditioning could certainly be improved, but overall it was a good stay.

author: Nichola B
title: AVOID if you’re travelling to New York as a family!
text:
Long review but a very honest review! I don’t normally review but this one I had to.

We stayed at this hotel for 5 nights at the beginning of August 2026 as part of my our 40th birthday trip. New York was our final stop after San Francisco, Las Vegas and Orlando, where we’d had fantastic experiences and amazing service. Unfortunately, this hotel was a completely different story and ended what had otherwise been an incredible trip on a very sour note.

Things went wrong almost immediately.

The hotel arranged for a a taxi transfer company to contact us to arrange pick up from the airport, which we thought would make things much easier after a long journey. The driver asked for our name and hotel, so we assumed everything was correct. We arrived at what we thought was our hotel, only for reception to tell us we were at the “other Hampton Inn.” We then had to collect all our luggage and walk to the correct hotel.
How would we have known there were other Hampton Inn hotels?! Surely the taxi transfer company knows this so why didn’t they ask us to be specific?! And why didn’t they know which one we were going to when the hotel arranged the contact? 

We were exhausted by the time we arrived, so despite everything, we decided not to complain and just wanted to get some food and go to bed.

Then we discovered one of the lifts was out of order. We were on the 16th floor, and it took around 15–20 minutes to get the remaining lift.

When we finally got to our room, we were genuinely shocked by how small it was. We were a family of four — two adults, a 14-year-old and a 9-year-old — and there was virtually no space at all. We couldn’t unpack because there simply wasn’t anywhere to put our belongings, so we had to live out of our suitcases for the entire stay.

The shower was also ridiculously small. My husband is 6ft 1 and actually banged his head several times while showering.

That first evening, we returned from dinner hoping to relax and watch some TV for an hour. The TV didn’t work.

We tried calling reception — the phone in our room didn’t work either.

That is particularly concerning when you are on the 16th floor and already have one lift out of service. In an emergency, being unable to contact reception from your room is a serious issue.

My husband went down to reception and reported the problems. We were told someone would come up.

By 10.30pm, we were exhausted and had to go to sleep.

The following day, we went out expecting that the issues would be sorted while we were away.

They weren’t.

When we returned, our room hadn’t been serviced at all. The towels we had used that morning were still on the floor, the beds hadn’t been made, and the TV was still not working.

I went down to reception and spoke to Andy, who apologised for everything — the wrong hotel transfer, the lift, the TV, the phone and the lack of room service.

He looked into moving us to a bigger room, but said there were no larger rooms available. He then offered Hilton points as compensation. As we aren’t Hilton members, this wasn’t particularly useful to us.

I asked whether there was any possibility of a refund so we could leave and stay somewhere else for the remaining four nights. Andy told me that this could be arranged, but that we needed to contact the company we had booked through. He explained that they would contact the hotel and the hotel would then confirm that we could leave and receive a refund.

At this point, we genuinely thought we were getting somewhere.

Unfortunately, the following morning my husband spoke to the General Manager, who told him that the information we had been given was incorrect and that we could not leave and receive a refund.

We were also told there were no larger rooms because the hotel doesn’t actually have larger rooms. So when Andy had looked into moving us to a bigger room, there was never actually a bigger room to move us to.

We were essentially stuck.

What disappointed us most was what happened afterwards. Following our conversation with the General Manager, not one member of staff checked in with us for the rest of our stay.

Not to ask if everything was okay.

Not to apologise.

Not to ask whether we wanted the Hilton points that had previously been offered.

Nothing.

On our final night, we returned to find that our room hadn’t been cleaned again, meaning we didn’t even have fresh towels for the following morning when we were flying home.

By that point, I honestly had no energy left to complain again.

Having now read back through some of the other reviews, I can see that comments about staff not seeming to care and problems being brushed aside are sadly very similar to our own experience.

This hotel completely let us down.

We will never stay here again, and although we absolutely love New York and will return, we will definitely be choosing a different hotel next time.

It’s such a shame because this was supposed to be a special 40th birthday trip. San Francisco, Las Vegas and Orlando had all been fantastic, with brilliant service throughout. Unfortunately, our experience here left us feeling incredibly disappointed and frustrated at the end of what had otherwise been an amazing holiday.

If you’re travelling to New York with a family, I would seriously recommend looking elsewhere.

author: Getaway11612799129
title: If you or someone you love has a disability or travel with a mobility device, read this before booking at this hotel.
text:
I stayed here in August 2026 while attending conferences nearby. My disability relapses unpredictably, and when symptoms returned a few weeks before the trip I tried to modify or cancel my reservation and could not, because I had booked through Expedia (which apparently forfeited all rights as a human). The hotel's website showed accessible rooms available that week, so I requested a low floor in the Hilton app and had my power chair delivered to the hotel ahead of my arrival.

Zay M. the front desk manager, checked me in arranged for my chair to be brought out to me at the front desk. Even so, I was never offered an accessible room. I had requested the 3rd floor and was assigned the 29th. No one said a word about any rules for the chair, including any rule against bringing it into my room, which is how I get around (and the manager even pointed to where the elevators where so I could access my room while I was in the chair).

The room's entryway was tight and there was a mirror in the entryway, and that evening the chair cracked the mirror. I reported it to the front desk myself within minutes and said I probably needed an ADA accommodation. The employee, Marwane, who answered responded with real care: they asked if I was okay, apologized that no accessible rooms were open that night, offered to remove the mirror and shift furniture so I could move safely, and promised to keep checking ADA availability. I said I could make do for the night. If it had ended there, this would be a different review.

Instead Zay M. took over the conversation and the tone turned accusatory. I was told I had never mentioned my mobility issues to him when I checked in. This is the same manager who had my power chair brought to me at check-in. I was told I should not have brought the chair into the room, and that I would pay for the mirror, later quoted to me at $400. It should be noted the hallway outside of the rooms are not wide enough to walk around if my chair was parked there.

I asked to speak with someone else and was told there was no one else and that he was the only manager. When I called Hilton's guest assistance line that evening, the representative checked with the hotel and came back saying I had been offered an ADA accommodation and declined it (probably in reference to my purchase on Expedia in March). That is not what happened, and it contradicts what the hotel's own staff had texted me an hour earlier.

I left that night, in a thunderstorm, and another hotel had an accessible room ready for me within an hour. Between the forfeited nights, the mirror charge, and a last-minute room elsewhere, this stay cost me well over a thousand dollars. It was my first trip without my caregiver for an academic conference that I am presenting at. I would much better have been preparing for that, than writing this review.

There was no understanding of ADA, no understanding of customer service, and there seemed to be way more interest in punishing and dehumanizing guests with disabilities than welcoming them.

title: 2nd Stay - Great Experience
text:

I was not an immediate fan of the resort fee but soon learned how to make the daily food credit in the hotel lounge work for me as the prices there are much more reasonable than food prices at Javits. 
The staff at this hotel is what brought me back for this return stay of 4 nights. They are really friendly and go out of their way to ask about your stay, room, check-in, and genuinely want to know if they can do anything for you. In my experience this is truly unique in hotels almost anywhere these days but particularly in New York City. I was literally greeted by name when I came through the lobby on several occasions!
Special shout out to front desk staff members Robbi and Jonathan for the extra attention and assistance and great efficiency . Also thanks to Neisha (overnight front desk) who took great care of me upon my very early morning arrival at the hotel until my room was ready. She was very gracious, supplied beverages and checked in frequently about my comfort and wellbeing. 
These are just the people I interacted with the most. All the staff members were friendly and efficient. This hotel delivers really well on all the basics but the staff sets the hotel apart and take the experience to another level!

The first was dirty at check in with a cookie still on the floor, crumbs all over the couch, and hairs on the sheets. The person sent to pick up the cookie told me that they did not have a working vaccum. The light was also out in the bathroom and because it was a Sunday so I was told they could not fix it. I had to move rooms. The windows are not double glazed so you can hear EVERYTHING from the blocks around. The breakfast is the slowest most ridiculous experience. I will not stay a 3rd time.

author: Cooper B
title: Absolutely the best!!
text: This is truly a hidden gem in the heart of Manhattan! The hotel is incredibly cozy, and the rooms are beautiful, comfortable, and thoughtfully designed. The staff is warm and welcoming, and the drinks and food are absolutely delicious. Everything was spotless, which made our stay even more enjoyable. I highly recommend this hotel and will definitely be coming back!

author: Lisa S
title: Lovely
text: Great location. Friendly staff. Lovely experience. Felt like a European boutique hotel. Highly recommend.

author: Kristen G
title: A hidden gem!
text:
We highly recommend the Merrion Row Hotel! As first-time visitors to New York City, we took a chance booking this boutique hotel on 45th Street, and it exceeded every expectation.

From the moment we arrived, the staff was incredibly friendly, welcoming, and went above and beyond to make our stay easy and comfortable. Our room was charming, cozy, spotless, and surprisingly quiet—such a peaceful retreat after busy days exploring the city.

We enjoyed breakfast at the restaurant downstairs twice, and it was excellent each time. Housekeeping was attentive, our room was always refreshed, and whenever we needed extra towels, they were delivered promptly.

One of the things we appreciated most was the exceptional hospitality. After we checked out, the staff graciously stored our luggage so we could enjoy a few more hours in the city before heading home, making our last day completely stress-free.

If you’re looking for a hotel with outstanding service, a unique boutique feel, and a fantastic location, the Merrion Row is a true gem. We would absolutely stay here again and would choose it over a large chain hotel any day. Thank you for making our first trip to NYC so memorable!

author: ian n
title: A change from the big chain hotels
text: Couldn’t be happier , we actually booked in next door at the Hyatt central but when we arrived they had double booked us so we were effectively shown the door (I did get the money back) whilst standing in the street with nowhere to go we seen Merrion , we called in and they had availability and checked us in, what a lovely little hotel, food was lovely , room was clean and very nice the staff are all super friendly and it was more than reasonable . Having stayed at a few hotels in NYC this is definitely the best and I’m pleased we were double booked next door and we will definitely be back and recommend to friends

author: leoniec585
title: Great expeeience
text: great location, great staff including Chris at Breakfast, Tamang and Shaddaf (not sure I have spelled correctly) at Reception and the lovely fellows helping with bags and taxis.

author: Hannah C
title: Lovely afternoon tea time
text: We had a lovely time at our Afternoon Tea today; in large part due to the amazing service we received from Adam! He did not rush us in any way, explained everything thoroughly and was extremely helpful when we needed it while not hovering. The scones were our favourite but the sandwiches and desserts were also delicious, especially the salmon sandwich and salted caramel dessert. The oolong pairs perfectly with the meal. The ambiance in the room is perfect. Decor is modern/art deco but also classic, just like the rest of The Dixon. Highly recommend.

author: Anainmiami
title: Perfect 5 Days in London
text: The hotel is lovely with all modern conveniences of elevators, air conditioning. The rooms are very comfortable & modern. The staff is warm and friendly. The restaurant staff is outstanding; Adam, Iris and Chris were always friendly and helpful at breakfast. They serve a wonderful buffet with a delicious variety of options. The location is also outstanding. A short walk to the Tower Bridge in one direction & the Underground in the other. This was a perfect locale for our 5 day holiday.

author: Julie S
title: Highly recommend
text: Beautiful hotel with wonderful service. Our hostess Iris remembered us daily and checked in about our travels. Very personable.

author: Emily A
title: High Tea Yums
text: High tea in the courtroom bar was excellent. Lina was the best. So kind and prompt.

author: Mark P
title: Great location for tube
text:
Location very good as tube station just a few minutes walk and a nice pub over the road and a nice restaurant connected to hotel.
The staff were lovely and friendly through out and helpful.
When we went to the rooms there was a strong smell of musty damp and this continued when we went in our room. 
The room itself was clean and tidy so no complaints there. we bought an air fresher and that did the trick for the musty smell.
The wi-fi was very bad but as only in room to sleep wasn't to mush of a problem if i had spent more time in hotel would of wanted the internet more.

author: Emmaharris2015
title: Good location and good food next door
text:
We chose this hotel as it was recommended on the Amex app with a deal.
The hotel is well situated and easy to get to with plenty of transport near by and amenities. 
The hotel is connected to a Chaiiwala restaurant which was lovely, and the breakfast included in the hotel payment was there, it was great each morning, coming with chicken sausages, turkey bacon, hashbrowns, beans, egg and toast. However, if you wanted English breakfast tea – it wasn’t an option and the teabags given were chai.
We love Indian food and they had a great choice for lunch.
You can also pay £5 each day to access the gym 2 doors down.
There are several pubs within walking distance, lots of takeaways and shops locally too.
The rooms are clean but very basic and in need of some modernisation. 

As we were visiting in summer, I was relieved to discover air conditioning which worked well! I would have appreciated some water in the room, when I asked the front desk whether I could get water he told me to go to Tesco or the local store. Even though I could see a fridge of bottles of water in the lobby. 
The bathroom was not the best, the door to the shower did not have adequate fittings and stayed open whilst showering, flooding the bathroom floor which we had to use our towels each day to soak up. The curtain track in the main room fell down every time we opened or closed the curtains. 
When we went out for the day, despite putting the housekeeping request on the door and switching on the designated light to indicate the room was ready to be cleaned, we would return to hotel around 3pm-4pm to get ready for our evenings and the rooms had not been turned down, had twice ran out of toilet roll and had no clean/dry towels to use, this happened every day. The rooms would be done by the time we returned at 10pm or so, but I really think that guests staying should be a priority. 

Immediate recommendations to elevate the hotel would be:
-	More milk sachets provided in room for teas and coffees.
-	Water in the rooms.
-	Wine glasses in the rooms for guests to use. 
-	Fix shower fittings. 
-	Fix curtain poles.
-	Get housekeeping to do service earlier in the day. 

Nevertheless, based on the location, the cost and the breakfast at Chaiiwala, I would consider staying again, its not the worst place to settle after long days out.

author: Kim C
title: Damp and smelly
text:
The location is handy for underground stations. We had a basement room and the room was just damp . The bedding and soft furnishings were all damp and it smelled really bad. We barely slept as we basically slept in a bed that was damp. 
there was a leak above the shower which was dripping constantly.

author: Emma L
title: Excellent hotel for the price
text:
This is our 5th time staying at the hotel and will definitely be returning. 
Our room was spacious and clean, with tea and coffee facilities. 
The bed was comfortable, providing us with a good nights sleep and the climate control was perfect, considering we visited during the recent heatwave.
Staff are friendly and helpful, greeting us with a cold lemonade on arrival.
Location is fantastic, 3 stops from Paddington which is great for exploring London.
We highly recommend as it’s such good value for money!

author: Sally W
title: Fabulous weekend in London
text: So my partner booked this hotel for our weekend in London to see Lewis Capaldi. London was very busy the weekend of 10th-12th July and we did pay over the odds. We had never stayed this side of London before and after reading the reviews it is safe to say I was very anxious and worried. When we arrived at Kilburn High road I was a bit concerned initially as I walked out, but once we had checked in and walked around we both really liked it. The receptionist was lovely and very friendly. We had a nice room, clean, working tv, working air con, clean bathroom no concerns AT ALL!  We always explore our area on arrival and it is clear other people don’t do the same. We found some cracking pubs on our doorstep, The Old Bell with a lovely outdoor area across the road and some other fab pubs in walking distance. We also found the wonderful  Paddington recreation ground just 10 minutes away. We have never had anything like this in London. A little cafe, kids play area, football courts, tennis courts, athletics track, large field where there was a cricket match taking place, forests and areas of nature, beautiful little gardens. We loved it that much we went for a walk the following morning before heading out for the day. The overground was 7 mins to Euston and everywhere else very easy to get around. Everyone we came across was polite end friendly and we loved it so much we would definitely return! We even went to one of the local pubs after the concert for the second half of the England quarter final football game along with extra time. The bar staff were so friendly and we had no issues at all. Absolutely fabulous weekend in London and would recommend, just keep an open mind. You are in a massive capital city at the end of the day! I appreciate everyone’s experiences are different but we can only comment on ours.

author: KateyKate
title: Great hotel, nice staff
text: Great location, nice room, lovely helpful staff

author: Travel03158040976
title: NCY adventure
text: I wanted to take a moment to express how absolutely incredible our stay was. Everything exceeded our expectations! The room was beautiful, far better than we could have ever imagined. The staff was incredibly welcoming and professional, making us feel at home from the very first moment. The breakfast was phenomenal and the value for money was truly unbelievable for such a prime location. Thank you for an unforgettable NYC adventure, we will definitely be recommending your hotel to everyone we know!!

author: JJH04
title: Good location, small rooms, but very clean
text:
Just had a nice two nights stay for a daughter mother trip to go see The Lost Boys. Location is very close to Amtrak and the bus station so good on that mark. About a 10 minute walk and you are in Times Square.
The rooms were clean, but small very small but again very clean. With two queen beds there wasn’t much room to move around, but we’re both adults and we weren’t spending all of our time in the room. Just wanted to forewarn anybody that’s traveling with small kids that needs more space. This may not be the place for you.
Hotel staff was very nice. Didn’t really have the breakfast, but the coffee wasn’t bad.

author: Francisco C
title: “Very disappointing experience — poor service and promises not kept”
text:
I had a very disappointing experience at SpringHill Suites by Marriott in Manhattan.

When I arrived, the room I had originally reserved was not available, so I was given a different room instead. Unfortunately, I had to stay in that room for the entire duration of my stay.

To make matters worse, during the first three nights, my room was not cleaned at all. The beds were not made and the towels were not changed. I complained to the front desk, and after raising the issue again, I was told that this should not have happened and that I would receive a $100 discount on my room as compensation.

However, when it was time to pay, I was told that there was no record of the $100 discount and that nothing could be done. This was extremely frustrating. If a member of the staff makes a commitment to a guest, it should be properly documented and honored. Otherwise, it becomes very difficult to trust what guests are being told.

I also found my interactions with Natasha, Jeffrey, Eric, and William to be particularly disappointing and unprofessional. Whenever I approached them to follow up on my complaints, I felt that I was simply being told “yes, yes, yes” to get me out of the way, without any genuine intention of resolving the problems.

Overall, the combination of being given a different room than the one I had booked, having no housekeeping service for the first three nights, and then being promised compensation that was not honored made this a very poor experience.

I expected much better from a Marriott property. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this hotel.

author: Robert H
title: I would return here
text:
This is standing Hotel for its price range and location! I would very much look forward to staying here again on my next visit to New York City. First, you can’t beat the location. If you desire, you can walk to Penn Station. Light many New York hotels, this was an old building that has been renovated. Whoever your interior designers are did an outstanding job of utilizing the space efficiently, designing the window treatments and artwork, and providing furnishings that are functional and comfortable. 

The dining area downstairs was done extremely well. The staff did a great job of making sure that the food was constantly replenished and this was  a very busy morning. Also, I forgot to mention that every place we went was spotless (with the exception of the small outdoor area  an occasional pigeon might visit).

author: Maureen T

author: Dale R

When I asked if he could clean up all the water in the bathroom he handed me towels and i had to dry it up myself. The staff are not helpfully at all and ill never stay there again. I have proof by the way

author: AF Travel
title: DISGUSTING HOTEL- DO NOT STAY
text:
I stayed in this hotel for one night and it was the  worst hotel I have ever stayed in. Unfortunately we had no other option otherwise we would have not endured this repulsive stay.

We were greeted at reception and it was extremely slow and nothing seemed to be working , it  took over half an hour to check in , the man on reception was extremely unfriendly and unwelcoming. The lobby was the cleanest part of the hotel and even then it wasn’t great!

They kept repeating that it was a non smoking hotel but our room stunk of cigarette smoke and the stains on the ceiling were evident of it.

When we arrived to the room the walls were covered in stains and the floor was covered in hair . The bathroom had not been cleaned and was falling apart , mouldy and disgusting.The floor,  carpet  , ceiling mattress were also covered in strange unpleasant stains . 

We went to reception to raise these concerned and were absolutely shocked and appalled to find ours and another guests check in paper work containing confidential details left out on the front desk for anyone to witness with no workers anywhere to be seen and they re appeared 10 minutes later from outside the building . This is an extreme breach of data protection and will be reporting this further .

When we did eventually speak to them about the issues we were met with attitude and dismissal , they moved us to the “best room” and it was just as foul. I will attach photos to this review to warn anyone to NEVER EVER stay in his hotel. They refused us a refund and wouldn’t acknowledge the absolute disgusting state the hotel is in.

I have no idea how this hotel is still open and charging the prices they do and is operating at such an extreme hygiene risk. DO NOT STAY HERE!

title: Satisfactory

Felt like it was smart once but has been left .
Reception area was tired  with wall paper coming away from wall .

That staffs deserve just as much praise.  Everyone was warm, attentive and extremely welcoming. Staffs would regularly check that everything was okay and making sure guests were well looked after.

Great food, excellent service and a genuinely lovely team.  A really positive experience at Premier Inn Victoria.

author: Ibrahim A
title: My amazing time at London Victoria premier Inn.

author: Jessica

author: AM
title: Excellent choice in the Financial District
text:
The hotel is not luxury, but for a week in New York it is more than fine. I liked the location a lot: during my first trip I had stayed in Times Square, but I must say that I definitely prefer the financial district. It is quieter, less noisy and allows you to easily reach the Stock Exchange, the World Trade Center, the harbor and other attractions.
The room was clean, also equipped with a small kitchenette. The beds were very comfortable, while the bathroom, although being a bit dated, was still in good condition. The view looked out onto another building, so nothing special.
The breakfast satisfied me: there was a good selection of both sweet and savory.
The only real negative note concerns the elevators, only two and rather dated. One evening I got stuck on the 30th floor: I recommend always carrying your cell phone with you and saving the reception number, because the alarm button doesn't inspire much confidence.

author: MLR
title: Don’t do it.
text:
This hotel truly disappoints.  No place to place your luggage.  No luggage stand. Privacy blinds you can see through? So you’re either in blackout drapes or everyone can see in.

Room size is honestly small.  Stay at the World Trade Center Marriot. Don’t stay here.

Elevators are a mess. This is not the place you want to stay.  Better deals and quality for the money.

See pic.  Asked for daily room service and after complaining about service with the on duty manager I didn’t get room service or luggage stand.   

Don’t do it.

author: Stephanie L

Thank you Pree!

author: AmyM487
title: Great value!
text: This was our first time to NYC and we thought this hotel was a great value! It is very close to a number of places to get a variety of food and an easy walk to the subway. We drove and used a parking garage that was only .2 miles from the hotel - there are several garages nearby. The rooms were clean and the beds comfortable. We didn't have the same issue with the elevators as another reviewer had and we found them to be quick. I would definitely stay here again.

author: Leticia_CL
title: Great cost benefit
text: The hotel is very well located, with many restaurants, snacks, markets nearby. Easy access to metro, to any part of the island. Comfortable room and good size, considering that in NY are very small. Only do not recommend breakfast at the hotel, as it is very expensive for what serves. Besides, I found a great choice.

author: Lesley W
title: Excellent accommodation.

Clean, spacious,  tasteful room.  Comfortable med firm bed,  double glazed, well equipped, kitchen, outside and inside seating. author: Maren D
title: Amazing

author: Victoria D

I felt a bit like i was at home, lovely shared spaces, did not feel crowded at all. It was very clean and had all the amenities we needed. Great location, close to the city by train, yet still quiet. Lots of stuff nearby too. 10/10 would recommended. thank you for a great stay

author: mayoharry
title: Comfortable stay
text:
I stay here whenever I visit my daughter who lives nearby.
Always comfortable and impeccably clean. Great to have use of 2 kitchen, lovely garden, sat in sunshine and chatted to the lovely Lisa. So friendly.
Always a pleasure to communicate with Tony also.
Will be back!

Thanks again for a great stay.

author: Herra R
title: Hidden Gem w/ wonderful Hosts :))
text:
We were very lucky to book our accommodation at this guesthouse. Tony, and his daughter Lisa are incredibly kind and welcoming, and their customer service is truly superb.
The room was lovely, clean, and very comfortable. We especially appreciated the beautiful garden, as well as the coffee supplies provided both in the room and in the kitchen.
What made our stay even better was the generous discount they gave us when we booked. It was a thoughtful gesture that we greatly appreciated.
Highly recommended! We would definitely stay here again and look forward to returning in the future. 😊

author: Shaiann S
title: I’ll be back

author: Aikaterini M
title: Great choice for visiting Paris
text: Great location, the Opera and Louvre are only 20 minutes by foot, Montmartre 15 minutes by foot too and so many other locations worth visiting are nearby. The room was clean and well equipped, the staff of the hotel is so friendly and we were offered everyday free snacks and drinks at the restaurant of the hotel and the minibar of our room. The price was a great deal. We definitely recommend it for Paris’ visitors.

author: Ernest G
text:
We had a really enjoyable stay at Hotel Joyce – Astotel during our trip to Paris. From the moment we arrived, the staff were friendly, welcoming and helpful, which made a great first impression.

The hotel itself was very clean and well maintained, and our room was comfortable and had everything we needed for our stay. After spending long days exploring Paris, it was a nice place to come back to and relax.

One of the things we particularly liked was the complimentary drinks and snacks available at the hotel. It was such a simple touch, but really appreciated after being out sightseeing for several hours. Breakfast was also good and gave us plenty of choice before heading out for the day.

The location worked really well for us too. There are restaurants and shops nearby, and it was easy enough to get around Paris using the Metro or by taxi.

Overall, Hotel Joyce was a great choice for our father-and-son trip. It felt welcoming, comfortable and well looked after throughout our stay. I would happily stay here again on another visit to Paris and would definitely recommend it to others.

5/5 – a lovely hotel and a very enjoyable stay.

author: PatrickF4438
title: Voyce on Joyce

author: Carlo T

Mauro and Simonetta.

author: Diego Esteban S

author: LauraD
title: Perfect family stay in Rome
text: We had the best stay here. From the moment we arrived we were welcomed with wide smiles and cold drinks. They could not have done enough for us. The rooms and hotel are decorated with stylish unique decor. Even the pool towels are unique per person. The neighbourhood is also really smart and very local. Lots of lively little restaurants and street corner bars. It’s a short bus ride to the centre so a perfect location for us to be away from the hustle and bustle. All round a 5* experience. Thank you Palm Gallery team

author: rickb366

Great hotel on the edge of Rome city centre.
Intimate, beautiful rooms, lovely roof terrace with swimming pool.

author: CriCri753
title: Location and hospitality

author: Linda
title: THIS is the place to stay
text: This is just the loveliest place, completely outside of the tourist area. That's important if you make the error of going to Rome during the tourist season. The room was very large and nice, old and clean, reeks of history in a good way. Bed comfy. Breakfast area, both indoor and outdoor, is just lovely. The rooftop pool and view are really nice. And oh, the flowers are everywhere. But the best, and I mean the best, is the wonderful owner. We arrived late in the evening, and our taxi driver tried to take advantage of us and charge an insane price. Well, the owner came and had it out with him, as he was trying to pull a fast one. She saved the day and got the price down to a reasonable cost. She was the BEST. And she and her staff were just so kind. We LOVED it there and would go back in a heartbeat. Extra added bonus...really delicious restaurants a block or so away. This place is a treat.

author: catia41
title: Dilapidated and incorrect.
text:
It is not a hotel, rather a b&b. That it is rated 4 stars is inconceivable then.
I marvel at the Tripadvisor ratings that I trusted blindly!
The room destined for us was in a part under renovation so uncomfortable and uncomfortable to get there, but the serious thing was the amount of dust present, the tiny size and a wall actually attached to the large front window compared to the bed! 
4.7 as an absurd Tripadvisor rating!
They gave us another larger room, but not well cleaned and with old furniture and not well maintained. The sheet embedded in the wood of the headboard of the bed was detached in several places and certainly not suitable even from a hygienic point of view.
Absurd!

author: stevehsimon
title: Not Hyatt Quality
text: This was not a quality Hyatt experience.    The hotel did not provide the upgraded room we booked even after considerable discussion.    The room we received was very small.   Hotel is on 9th avenue so not very centrally located.    There were too few working elevators which made the wait time to go to or from your room a consideration.   The lobby was jammed with people because it was undersized for the number of people in the hotel.    Wished we had stayed in the Embassy Suites which was the same price, centrally located and generally more comfortable.   I would not recommend this hotel.

author: Morgan A
title: Excellent location
text: Great hotel. Excellent location close to Times Square and the subway. Very clean. Friendly and professional staff. Would definitely stay here again.

author: Tondee L
title: Very Friendly / Hot Room
text: The hotel is clean and modern and the staff are friendly.   be prepared that the breakfast is very very busy and closes ridiculously early - at 9:30 during the week. We ended up only going one day on our three day stay. The worst part of this stay was how hot our room was and it didn’t seem there was anything they could do about it. Thermostat doesn’t go lower than 68 but there’s no way it was below 70 in our room and it was very warm at night when we were trying to sleep.

author: dona79
title: A stone's throw from Times Square
text: Hotel on a side street a stone's throw from Times Square and the subway. Clean but tiny room, microscopic bathroom with a shower without hot water... If you are lucky, maybe it gets lukewarm😩 Elevators almost always full and a long wait, but I think they are like that a bit everywhere in New York. Breakfast was neither good nor bad: scrambled eggs, bacon, fruit, bread, and bagels to toast with jams and butter, coffee, and juices. Go early or you won't get a seat.

author: Immy L
title: Good but don't expect anything great!
text: I was a guest with a disability and specifically requested interconnecting rooms when booking so our family of five could stay together. Additionally, as this trip was a birthday celebration, my wife asked if the hotel could do anything to make the occasion special. Unfortunately, the hotel failed to acknowledge either request. As a loyal Hyatt guest who has stayed at properties worldwide, this first experience in NYC was deeply disappointing, making me hesitant to book with Hyatt again. During our trip, we visited the Ritz-Carlton Central Park for light birthday refreshments and were blown away by their service. While I realize the Hyatt is a 4-star property compared to the Ritz’s 5-star standard, basic acknowledgement of our requests would have made a world of difference.

author: Szilvia O
title: Elevator
text: The hotel itself has a good location, but the breakfadt is horrible( not a vegitable or a ham or sousage, only egg and sweet items) the elevators are out of order almost every day, our room was on 9th floor.The city view is a lie , we were seeing a nother building 🥲The staff is ok!Compare to the price we paid i think the hotel should provide better service thinking more about the European guests!

author: corbes63
title: Excellent stay!
text:
We nearly didn't book this hotel because the reviews seemed a bit hit-and-miss, but we're very glad we did. We’ve previously stayed in a bunch of different places around town.
Pros:
No “destination/resort” fee!
The location felt really safe throughout our stay, and there is visible security around reception during the overnight hours. The hotel is in a nice neighbourhood, just a few minutes' walk from the subway, making it easy to get around the city and away from the crazy of Times Square.
Breakfast was genuinely excellent and far exceeded our expectations. The hotel arranged gluten-free bagels for us on request at check-in, which was greatly appreciated after our emails prior to the stay went unanswered. There was a wide variety of rotating hot and cold options each morning, and honestly, the breakfast was better than what I've experienced in many executive lounges at full-service US hotel brands. The breakfast team worked incredibly hard keeping everything stocked and refreshed, even during the busiest periods.
Housekeeping was fantastic. They always respected the Do Not Disturb sign and never interrupted us unnecessarily. Gloria deserves special recognition for doing an amazing job freshening up our room when we needed service.
Bryant on the afternoon/evening reception shift was also lovely, and incredibly helpful throughout our stay. A special thank you as well to the manager, Dawn, who was outstanding from start to finish and made a real difference to our experience.
One concern we had before arriving was reports of construction noise, but we didn't see or hear any construction during our stay. We actually stayed in two different rooms and both were exceptionally quiet, with no outside noise at all. Some rooms also feature a double-door arrangement that helps reduce noise from the hallway and other guests. With only around 10 rooms per floor, the hotel felt quiet.
Air conditioning was excellent, we had a heat wave whilst there and the rooms were lovely and cool.
And for anyone wondering from a previous review —we checked carefully and found absolutely no signs of bed bugs.
The guest laundry facilities were also very useful, with a single washing machine and dryer available for guests.
As for the negatives, room sizes do vary slightly by shape but are compact as advertised and reported.
Some reception staff were grumpy and unhelpful, which was inconsistent compared to the excellent service we received from others.
Also, one elevator appears to be permanently out of service, leaving only a single lift operating. If you're staying on a higher floor, it's worth allowing extra time, especially during busy periods.
Breakfast can also get quite busy, and you may occasionally need to wait a minute for a table, although the breakfast staff do an outstanding job keeping everything refreshed and flowing smoothly.
Overall this was a great stay for us. The excellent breakfast, quiet rooms, convenient location, strong housekeeping team, and standout staff members made this a very enjoyable stay, and we would happily stay here again. Many thanks to Dawn and the team!

author: Rabbul M
title: Do not recommend
text:
As a Marriott Lifetime member, this is probably one of the worst hotels, not just within the Marriott brand but among all the hotels I’ve stayed at.

I booked a high-floor room, but at check-in I was told none were available. The room had no complimentary water, and when I asked about it, I was told that water is provided “at the hotel’s discretion.” I was eventually given two tiny bottles.

To make matters worse, the room didn’t have air conditioning. Charging nearly $400 per night for a room without AC is simply unacceptable. The lack of basic amenities, combined with poor service and untrained staff, made this an extremely disappointing stay.

author: Experience819960
title: The elevator is a major issue
text: I am currently staying here. The elevator issue is a major problem. I wasn't notified upon check in that my room would be directly  across from the elevator and that I would hear a  clicking noise all night long. I tried to switch rooms the next day but I had online meetings and didnt have a minute to switch at that time. I tried to switch in the evening but all rooms were sold out. I had conversations with the guy who had to sit in the elevator pushing buttons all day and night and he mentioned they were servicing the elevator we were using next week. This is a major issue:(

author: Traveller From London
title: Worst Marriott experience I've ever had in my life - after being Titanium Elite for 10 years
text:
One of the worst hotels I have ever stayed at in my life. I am Marriott Titanium Elite. They were extremely difficult about providing an early check in - even at 1:30PM. The lady who checked me in even lied and said they were sold out so couldnt switch me to a king bed room, despite there being plenty of rooms on sale online. How can they not clean even 1 room between the check out time of 11AM and 1:30PM? I don't expect this inability to provide a room given my loyalty status. 

Only 1 elevator works and takes forever!! The working elevator causes so much noise I can hear it go up and down loudly from inside of my room - its woken me up so many times that my whoop sleep score is the lowest I've ever seen it. 

There is EXTREMELY LOUD DRILLING construction on the road in front of the hotel - i guess this is not their fault, but they should warn guests. The walls are thin and you can hear every single thing outside the room - even if people are chatting you can hear ever word. 

Room is tiny and generally quite awful, even for NYC standards. I presumed it would be bigger given this is a suite hotel, but I didnt check the measurements beforehand. Its basically the same as a Moxy. If you are overweight, you definitely will not fit in the bathroom.

author: glasgowgals
title: Still the best!
text:
Having visited this accommodation many years ago. I knew what to expect and as always it hit the mark.
The room was  big  and comfy, air con , great wardrobe and storage , fab shower and a wee fridge too it was ideal.
Wi-Fi connectivity was brilliant too.
The location is in a great district. Lots of facilities around the corner. 
And a stroll to the Vatican and Castel Angelo.

Luca and his son are charming and helpful hosts. 
Our taxi he arranged to the airport was superb, prompt service lovely car. Driven by Roberta.

We will be back. Ciao !

author: Sarah B
title: 10 out of 5 stars
text: We had an absolutely wonderful stay at Rome Armony Suites. The room we stayed in was a large family room which was cleaned daily and had bottled water left each day which was very kind. We travelled as a family and found it a safe, lovely area to stay in, so close to all the major tourist sites that we walked to the Vatican and used the subway for further travels with no issues. Luca was an exceptional host who helped us with everything. He gave us assistance in finding allergy friendly and gluten free places to eat. He booked transfers for us to and from the airport and the drivers did a fantastic job. There was a massive traffic jam on the way to the airport and our driver went miles out of his way through countryside so we made our flight. Likewise, the breakfast place he booked for us each day was very convenient and we really liked it. We really loved our stay and cannot recommend it enough as a place to stay. Many many thanks !!

author: Domenic S
title: Luca is the Best!
text:
Luca is one of the nicest people I’ve ever met
Very detailed and cares deeply about your stay
Location is perfect. Very safe and quiet neighborhood 
About 15 min walk to Vatican, 50 min walk to coliseum, 30 min walk to piazza navona 
Room is clean and easy to rest in
If he offers the airport pickup, take it!  Mercedes Benz for reasonable rate 
Definitely will stay here again when I return to Rome

author: Tracy
title: Our new favorite hotel in Rome
text:
First let me say that I traveled internationally for most of my career and I have stayed in hundreds of 5 star hotels with tons of amenities. While this is not a 5 star hotel, Luca and his family provided the best customer service of any hotel I have ever experienced. His dedication to his clients is the best ever, bar none. The room was immaculately clean, well-appointed, with the biggest bed I have ever seen. The location is perfect; close enough to walk to the Vatican, the Spanish steps, and other famous attractions, but in a real neighborhood. It is the perfect balance for those who love to experience cities the way a local experiences them. 
Luca gave us suggestions for tours and attractions that we never would have considered but are delighted that he told us about. His restaurant recommendations were perfect. We had delicious food at great prices. We were there for a week and we will be coming back before we fly home. 
When I couldn’t figure out how to book a train ticket online (Italian train tickets  are clunky using  their website and hard to understand) Luca handled it all for me before I even arrived. His knowledge of the city and its attractions is invaluable and his patience and kindness are unparalleled. I told him that I had read a negative review and fell in love with him based upon his intelligent and hilarious response. Clearly the person writing that review was a jealous competitor. 
If the rating scale goes to 5 stars, this place is a solid 10. We feel like we have made a friend for life. If you are considering this hotel for your trip to Rome, book now. You will be elated that you made the right choice!

author: Marta
title: Stay by Luca!
text:
Staying with Luca was a pleasant surprise in the capital!
Highly recommended for services, room, location and especially for advice on what to see and where to eat!
The location is quiet convenient to the Vatican and Lepanto metro, the clean room with XXXL bed😄, spacious shower, bedroom slippers and bottle of water on the bedside table every day (much appreciated)
Thanks Luca!

author: catherine m
title: VERY GOOD HOTEL
